sections.title: Three ways to say "how much"
sections.content: Hungarian has three common intensifiers that go right before the word they intensify: nagyon ("very") is strong and neutral, elég ("quite, fairly") is more moderate, and túl ("too") means an excessive amount — you already met túl describing sizes that don't fit. Combine any of them with a weather or season word: nagyon meleg ("very warm"), elég szeles ("quite windy"), túl hideg ("too cold").

items.english: In spring the weather is quite windy.

sections.content: elég also means "enough" on its own (Ez elég. — "This is enough."). As an intensifier right before an adjective it softens to "quite/fairly": elég meleg ("quite warm"), not "enough warm".
